newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Treasurer says deals threaten muni market.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Treasurer says deals threaten muni market.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong said Thursday that a series of controversial municipal securities transactions threatened the integrity of the municipal market.

At a meeting of the California Debt Advisory Commission in Sacramento, Fong released letters calling on the Securities and Exchange Commission and the state Attorney General to investigate the transactions. He also released an informal opinion by the state Attorney General about the deals.
In addition, the commission adopted disclosure guidelines related to land-based debt securities.

The commission said the guidelines were developed to assist public officials in developing disclosure documents that fulfill their requirements under law and minimize their exposure to fraud liabilities.
Among its recommendations, the commission said developers should be primarily responsible for the flow of information to the secondary market concerning the status of developments.

Fong said the guidelines should help to protect investors and homeowners. He said he would also convene a taskforce with the state Department of Corporations and Attorney General on how to deal with any abuses in future deals.

Fong called on the SEC and Attorney General to investigate nine bond deals underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc. The transactions were conducted under the state's Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, authorizing the formation of joint powers agencies to finance the capital projects of local governments.

In these transactions, the joint powers agencies were formed by local governments in return for a cash payment from the bond proceeds. The bond proceeds were represented as being used to pay for public capital improvements in other areas of the state but in fact were first used to retire loans against the developer's private property, Fong alleged.
"In my view, these practices violate state laws, raise federal securities law concerns, and harm the interests of the issuer community in general," Fong said.
An Attorney General's opinion released Thursday confirmed Fong's assessment of the transactions, Fong's office said.

"Abuse of the Marks-Roos Act threatens the integrity of the municipal market, and by this opinion, the state Attorney General confirms our suspicions," Fong said. "Now we need to take the necessary steps beyond this opinion to prevent further abuses from taking place."
